classes.label: Domain Record
classes.definition: A versioned domain record with source identity, scope and independent evidence-status dimensions.

classes.label: Project
classes.definition: The job or development to which buildings, reports, approvals and work belong.

classes.label: Building
classes.definition: A physical building within a project; a project may contain several buildings.

classes.label: Building Part
classes.definition: An identifiable building part with its own use and assessment context.

classes.label: Location
classes.definition: The report's spatial description, preserving wording and keeping failure and damage locations distinct.

classes.label: Building Element
classes.definition: A physical component discussed by the report, with recorded or candidate identity and location.

classes.label: Construction System
classes.definition: How recorded elements work together in a system; not inferred from similarity alone.

classes.label: Material
classes.definition: A material explicitly mentioned or identified by the source.

classes.label: Product
classes.definition: A proprietary product or assembly where recorded; unknown products remain unknown.

classes.label: Interface
classes.definition: A sourced junction or interface between elements, such as a membrane-to-wall termination.

classes.label: Building Use
classes.definition: Documented use of a building or part, retained as evidence rather than automatic classification.

classes.label: Environmental Condition
classes.definition: A recorded environmental condition, including exposure or habitable space below.

classes.label: Construction Condition
classes.definition: A recorded construction condition, such as height, construction type or internal/external context.

classes.label: Assessment
classes.definition: An attributable assessment with premises, source, purpose and qualifications.

classes.label: Classification Assessment
classes.definition: An assessment of a particular subject using a stated classification definition and context.

classes.label: Building Classification Assessment
classes.definition: A building/part classification assessment; never propagated to other parts without support.

classes.label: Classification Definition
classes.definition: An editioned original definition and exceptions used by a reviewed classification assessment.

classes.label: Building Class
classes.definition: A building or building-part class in its code/jurisdiction definition; distinct from finish and membrane classes.

classes.label: Concrete Finish Class
classes.definition: A concrete surface finish classification in its specification or standard context.

classes.label: Membrane Class
classes.definition: A membrane classification in its product or standard context.

classes.label: Work Event
classes.definition: Original construction, alteration or recorded repair with affected scope, dates and outcome evidence.

classes.label: Original Construction
classes.definition: The original construction event, separate from subsequent or proposed work.

classes.label: Alteration
classes.definition: A later alteration with its own scope, approval and applicability context.

classes.label: Repair Event
classes.definition: A repair reported or recorded as undertaken; a recommendation alone cannot create this event.

classes.label: Proposed Remedial Work
classes.definition: Proposed remedial work, kept separate from undertaken repairs and original construction.

classes.label: Work Package
classes.definition: A particular construction or remedial work scope used by an assessment context.

classes.label: Assessment Context
classes.definition: The building part, work purpose, jurisdiction, dates and approval pathway for a question.

classes.label: Project Fact
classes.definition: A sourced project fact or attributed user declaration, retaining conflicts and unknown values.

classes.label: Approval Record
classes.definition: A consent, certificate, stamped drawing or declared design; source statements do not erase contrary observations.

classes.label: Compliance Certificate
classes.definition: An attributable statement of certification with recorded scope and source.

classes.label: Inspection Record
classes.definition: An inspection's recorded observations, author, dates and scope.

classes.label: Performance Solution Record
classes.definition: A documented Performance Solution with stated scope and evidence; existence cannot be inferred from a DTS departure.

classes.label: Source Document
classes.definition: A report, original authority, drawing, specification, manufacturer instruction, certificate or inspection document.

classes.label: Document Version
classes.definition: An immutable document version, distinct from editions it mentions.

classes.label: Report Version
classes.definition: A particular expert report version whose authored opinions and observations remain attributable.

classes.label: Drawing
classes.definition: A project drawing with identifier, revision and source scope.

classes.label: Specification
classes.definition: A project specification, distinguished from code adoption and manufacturer guidance.

classes.label: Manufacturer Instruction
classes.definition: An identified manufacturer's instruction and its product/edition context.

classes.label: Code Family
classes.definition: A BCA/NCC document family, separate from its editions and volumes.
classes.source_section: Australian Standard editions and reference relationships

classes.label: Code Edition
classes.definition: A specific BCA/NCC published edition and amendment; publication alone does not establish adoption or applicability.
classes.source_section: Australian Standard editions and reference relationships

classes.label: Code Volume
classes.definition: An edition-specific volume with its own identity and source coverage; building class alone does not select it.
classes.source_section: Australian Standard editions and reference relationships

classes.label: Jurisdiction Provision
classes.definition: A separately sourced jurisdiction variation or effective/adoption provision.
classes.source_section: Australian Standard editions and reference relationships

classes.label: Standard Family
classes.definition: An Australian Standard family, such as AS 4654, separate from parts and editions.
classes.source_section: Australian Standard editions and reference relationships

classes.label: Standard Part
classes.definition: A particular standard part; AS 4654.1 and AS 4654.2 are not interchangeable.
classes.source_section: Australian Standard editions and reference relationships

classes.label: Standard Edition
classes.definition: A specific part/year/amendment identity; reported citations remain unverified until original source review.
classes.source_section: Australian Standard editions and reference relationships

classes.label: Reference Relationship
classes.definition: An editioned, scoped reference link with explicit basis, conditions, exceptions and verification state.
classes.source_section: Australian Standard editions and reference relationships

classes.label: Reference Chain
classes.definition: A sequence of independently assessed primary, secondary or further reference links.
classes.source_section: Australian Standard editions and reference relationships

classes.label: Source Fragment
classes.definition: An identified clause, table, figure, appendix, definition, note or detail in a specific source edition.

classes.label: Clause
classes.definition: A clause or subclause with parent, definitions, conditions, exceptions and original context.

classes.label: Table
classes.definition: A table with its headers, notes, units and original reading structure.

classes.label: Figure
classes.definition: A source figure with labels, dimensions, interfaces and original context.

classes.label: Appendix
classes.definition: An appendix with its recorded normative/informative role.

classes.label: Definition
classes.definition: An editioned definition used by a requirement or classification assessment.

classes.label: Note
classes.definition: A source note retained with its provision; its role is not automatically mandatory.

classes.label: Guidance
classes.definition: Informative guidance, commentary or examples distinguished from mandatory provisions.

classes.label: Drawing Detail
classes.definition: An identified project drawing detail with its drawing and revision identity.

classes.label: Legal Provision
classes.definition: A cited legal provision with jurisdiction/version and source; report opinions are not binding legal determinations.

classes.label: Requirement
classes.definition: A required outcome under an established source basis and assessment context.

classes.label: Performance Requirement
classes.definition: A Performance Requirement considered in a compliance assessment.

classes.label: DTSProvision
classes.definition: A DTS provision considered separately from a Performance Requirement or documented Performance Solution.

classes.label: Compliance Assessment
classes.definition: A finding/evidence assessment against considered requirements and a recorded compliance pathway.

classes.label: Applicability Assessment
classes.definition: A context-specific supported, excluded or unresolved applicability decision using sourced facts and reviewed rules.
classes.source_section: Australian Standard editions and reference relationships

classes.label: Defect Item
classes.definition: An authored topic grouping that can contain distinct occurrences and explicitly shared reasoning.

classes.label: Defect Occurrence
classes.definition: A particular finding scoped to report/version/schedule, element and recorded location; repeated IDs are not merged automatically.

classes.label: Observation
classes.definition: What the source records at a finding or stated shared scope, retaining method and attribution.

classes.label: Test Measurement
classes.definition: A source reading, dimension or test with value, units, method, instrument and conditions as written; OCR remains uncertain.

classes.label: Expert Assessment
classes.definition: An author's conclusion about a condition or departure with source-backed premises.

classes.label: Occurrence Extent Assessment
classes.definition: An authored specific/recurring/systemic distribution assessment, separate from physical severity and statutory status.

classes.label: Status Assessment
classes.definition: An authored major/non-major or other status with its cited basis and reasoning; element status alone is insufficient.

classes.label: Severity Assessment
classes.definition: A physical severity assessment, independent of occurrence extent and statutory major-defect status.

classes.label: Cause Assessment
classes.definition: An attributable confirmed, suspected, alternative or unresolved explanation; possible causes are not independently confirmed diagnoses.

classes.label: Consequence Assessment
classes.definition: An attributable existing or predicted consequence, retaining the distinction from a failure's location.

classes.label: Reasoning
classes.definition: The author's premises and reasoning connecting observations, history, construction and considered requirements.

classes.label: Application Inference
classes.definition: A later application inference with explicit premises, separate from report-authored reasoning.

classes.label: Remediation Option
classes.definition: A source-authored proposed repair option with its scope, sequence, prerequisites, limitations and alternatives.

classes.label: Remediation Scope
classes.definition: The source's complete repair scope and qualifications, including wider reinstatement alternatives.

classes.label: Remediation Step
classes.definition: A source-listed proposed action in its authored order; a step is not evidence it was implemented.

classes.label: Prerequisite
classes.definition: A source-stated condition such as design, consent, access, manufacturer confirmation or temporary accommodation.

classes.label: Verification Criterion
classes.definition: An acceptance/verification criterion supplied by a source or separately reviewed proposal.

classes.label: Party
classes.definition: A named party with recorded identity; role or report proximity does not establish responsibility.

classes.label: Party Role
classes.definition: A recorded builder, architect, certifier or waterproofer role, kept separate from a resolved named party.

classes.label: Appointment
classes.definition: A sourced appointment and scope linking a particular party to work or a project.

classes.label: Responsibility Assessment
classes.definition: An authored responsibility attribution with work scope, reasoning and source; distinct from physical cause or legal determination.

classes.label: Authorship
classes.definition: An attributable document/statement author identity and recorded date.

classes.label: Original Asset
classes.definition: Preserved original bytes identified by content hash, separately from every meaningful occurrence.

classes.label: Image Asset
classes.definition: Original image bytes; identical bytes can be reused without merging occurrences or contexts.

classes.label: Image Occurrence
classes.definition: Where an image appears, its caption, source location, role and qualified finding/shared context.

classes.label: Depicted Fragment
classes.definition: The identified source fragment depicted by an image; identification is separate from original-source verification and applicability.

classes.label: Text Passage
classes.definition: An exact anchored native or OCR source span, retaining offsets and content kind.

classes.label: OCRExtraction
classes.definition: OCR output with regions, reading order, method and uncertainty; it cannot alone establish original governing text.

classes.label: Diagram Extraction
classes.definition: Attributed labels, interfaces, dimensions and relationships extracted from an original diagram.

classes.label: Image Annotation
classes.definition: A highlight, arrow, crop or comment kept distinguishable from original source content.

classes.label: Reported History
classes.definition: Attributable reported history, including instructed facts and repair accounts, distinct from direct observation.

classes.label: Logical Unit
classes.definition: A structural source grouping used to preserve occurrence or explicitly shared item context.

classes.label: Evidence Chunk
classes.definition: A searchable evidence revision with exact source segments; a chunk does not receive its own ontology.

classes.label: Qualified Assertion
classes.definition: A relation reified with subject, object, source spans, scope and independent evidence/review/verification/applicability/outcome dimensions.

classes.label: Knowledge Gap
classes.definition: Missing, conflicting or unresolved evidence, distinguished from proof that a document or event does not exist.

classes.label: Reviewed Rule
classes.definition: An explicit sourced/versioned applicability or classification rule requiring reviewer and regression-case validation before activation.

classes.label: Search Concept
classes.definition: A governed discovery term and aliases; similarity or alias matching cannot mint a factual cause, class or adoption link.

constraints.rule: Every factual relation has owned source spans/structural membership and explicit occurrence/item/context scope.
Building, concrete finish and membrane class identifiers are not equivalent.
Finding IDs are scoped to report/version/schedule; repeated identifiers produce review gaps, not automatic merges.
Publication/citation year alone never establishes adoption or applicability.
Review does not change an authored opinion into an observation or binding legal determination.
Governing/classification decisions require original source support, reviewed rules and a specific assessment context.
A remediation option/step cannot imply a repair was undertaken or effective.
OCR/image identification stays separate from original-source verification and applicability.
Keep source values and units; do not infer moisture percentages or resolve uncertain decimals.
Reference basis, edition/part/amendments, conditions and exceptions remain explicit.
Similarity and alias matching produce discovery mappings, not causal, classification or adoption facts.
Unavailable evidence is not proof a document or event does not exist.
